# Working of Binary Search

#### Course: DSA with C++

## Working of Binary Search

Suppose we have the following sorted vector, and we have to find the index of element 4 (the target value).

![A Sorted vector](data:image/png;base64,)

1. Divide the vector into two parts.

Consider, low is the index of the first element of the scope and high is the index of the last element of the scope.

![Set Low and High](data:image/png;base64,)

Now we need to divide our vector into two equal halves. So, we split the vector over the middle

element.

![Find the mid Index](data:image/png;base64,)

- If the mid element is the target element, we have found our target.

- If the target is smaller than the mid element, we narrow the scope of the target element to the left side of the mid element.

- If the target is greater than the mid element, we narrow the scope of the target to the right side of the mid element.

We repeat this process until we find our target element or the length of the search scope falls down to zero.

2. Repeat for the left side.

Since our target element 4 is less than the middle element 6, we repeat the steps on the lower halves (elements to the left of the middle element).

![Update the high Index](data:image/png;base64,)

Again, we divide the vector into two halves and compare our target element with the middle element.

This time, the target element is equal to the middle element. Hence, our search is completed.

![Found the Target Element](data:image/png;base64,)
